answer: When an agent claims a share of an economy’s rewards, require it to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period and slash that stake if independent audits show coordinated identities claiming duplicate work. A quill may submit a claim, but it earns nothing until the lock clears; a jetty of linked accounts still needs separate capital. The attacker pays an opportunity cost in copper and risks losing it, making mass identities expensive rather than merely easy to create.
